adaptation_measures: Shift farm labor to early morning or late afternoon and provide water/rest breaks.
Increase irrigation or moisture conservation for heat-sensitive crop stages.
Provide shade, ventilation, and water for livestock and poultry.

texts.bulletin: DANGEROUS HEAT STRESS — Piat: WBGT index in danger zone. SUSPEND all field work from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Ensure field workers rest in shade and drink water every 15 minutes. Monitor livestock — ensure shade, ventilation, and clean water for poultry/swine. Coordinate with RHU/BHS on heat-related illness protocols. Apply irrigation to vegetable crops early morning or late afternoon only.
texts.sms: DA HEAT ALERT: Dangerous heat in Piat. NO farm work 9AM-4PM. Drink water. Protect livestock.
texts.lgu:
HEAT STRESS EMERGENCY — Piat
WBGT index in dangerous range.
1. Issue public health advisory with RHU.
2. Restrict field labor 9AM–4PM.
3. Coordinate BAI for livestock heat stress monitoring.
4. Ensure water availability at farm sites.
texts.facebook:
🌡️ HEAT DANGER ALERT — Piat

Mapanganib na init ngayon!
⛔ Huwag magtrabaho sa bukid mula 9AM–4PM
💧 Uminom ng maraming tubig
🐔 Bantayan ang mga hayop

#HeatStress #DARFOCagayanValley

texts.bulletin: OPERATIONS ADVISORY - DEFER HARVESTING - Cabagan: manual harvest, combine harvest, hauling from field should be deferred. Recommended action: defer harvest or machine entry until fields can carry workers and equipment safely.

3. Coordinate BAI for livestock heat stress monitoring.
4. Ensure water availability at farm sites.

adaptation_measures: Coordinate field validation with MAO/AEWs before public release.
Prioritize advisories for vulnerable rainfed and smallholder production areas.
Document farm impacts for DA and PCIC support where losses are observed.

texts.bulletin: OPERATIONS ADVISORY - DEFER OPEN-AIR GRAIN DRYING - Cordon: sun-drying of palay or corn grain should be deferred. Basis: rainfall increases runoff, wash-off, grain wetting, or harvest loss risk; high humidity slows drying and increases mold or grain-quality risk. ACAP calendar anchor: Jun 16-30 - Rice season 2 - Planting / Newly planted; Corn season 2 - Seedling. Recommended action: avoid open sun-drying; use covered temporary storage or mechanical drying where available.
texts.sms: DA OPS: Defer open-air grain drying in Cordon. Rainfall increases runoff, wash-off, grain wetting, or harvest loss risk. Check MAO guidance.
texts.lgu:
OPERATIONS ADVISORY - DEFER OPEN-AIR GRAIN DRYING - Cordon
Operation: sun-drying of palay or corn grain
Why defer: rainfall increases runoff, wash-off, grain wetting, or harvest loss risk; high humidity slows drying and increases mold or grain-quality risk.
ACAP calendar: Jun 16-30 - Rice season 2 - Planting / Newly planted; Corn season 2 - Seedling.
LGU/MAO action: avoid open sun-drying; use covered temporary storage or mechanical drying where available; inform affected barangays and reschedule support services.
texts.facebook: Operations Advisory - Defer Open-Air Grain Drying - Cordon: Please defer sun-drying of palay or corn grain for now. Reason: rainfall increases runoff, wash-off, grain wetting, or harvest loss risk. Current crop calendar basis: Rice season 2 - Planting / Newly planted; Corn season 2 - Seedling. Coordinate with your Municipal Agriculturist for the next safe field window.
texts.bulletin: HIGH HEAT STRESS — Cordon: Avoid prolonged field work from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM. Ensure adequate hydration for farm workers. Monitor heat-sensitive crops (vegetables, high-value crops). Reschedule spraying and transplanting to early morning hours. Check livestock ventilation and water supply.
texts.sms: DA ADVISORY: High heat in Cordon. Avoid farm work 10AM-2PM. Stay hydrated.
texts.lgu:
HEAT STRESS ADVISORY — Cordon
High heat conditions: schedule farm work early morning or late afternoon.
texts.facebook: ☀️ HEAT ADVISORY — Cordon: High heat conditions. Avoid fieldwork 10AM–2PM. #DARFOCagayanValley #HeatStress

texts.bulletin: DANGEROUS HEAT STRESS — Santiago City: WBGT index in danger zone. SUSPEND all field work from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Ensure field workers rest in shade and drink water every 15 minutes. Apply irrigation to vegetable crops early morning or late afternoon only.

texts.bulletin: Harvest disruption risk in Uyugan due to rainfall of 36.5 mm/24h. Farmers in ripening or harvesting stages should: (1) Defer combine harvester deployment to avoid bogging; (2) Protect cut stalks from further wetting; (3) Prioritize mechanical drying over sun-drying for collected grain. Postharvest drying risk is ELEVATED. Coordinate with DA mechanization service providers for mobile dryer access.
texts.sms: DA ADVISORY: Rain risk for harvest in Uyugan. Defer harvest, use mechanical dryer if available. Call MAO for help.
texts.lgu:
HARVEST ADVISORY — Uyugan
Rainfall of 36.5 mm may disrupt ongoing harvest operations.
Recommended actions:
1. Advise farmers to assess field conditions before deploying machinery.
2. Coordinate with RCEF mechanization pool for mobile dryer deployment.
3. Issue tarpaulin assistance where needed.
4. Document areas where harvest was deferred for scheduling follow-up.
texts.facebook:
🌧️ HARVEST ADVISORY — Uyugan

Rain is affecting harvest conditions. Delay harvesting if fields are wet. Use mechanical dryers to prevent grain spoilage.

📞 Contact your Municipal Agriculturist for drying support.
#Palay #Mais #Harvest #DARFOCagayanValley
